message.content:
Below is a concise list of the **federal statutory holidays that create long‑weekend breaks in Canada for 2023**.  
(If you need provincial‑specific holidays, let me know and I can add those too.)

| Long‑Weekend Period | Holiday(s) Involved | Notes |
|---------------------|---------------------|-------|
| **Jan 1 – Jan 3** | New Year’s Day (observed on Monday, Jan 2) | New Year’s Day falls on Sunday; the observed day is Monday, giving a 3‑day break. |
| **Apr 7 – Apr 9** | Good Friday (Apr 7) → Easter Monday (Apr 9) | Good Friday is a statutory holiday; Easter Monday is a federal holiday in some provinces but not federally observed. However, the 3‑day stretch is still a long weekend for many Canadians. |
| **May 20 – May 22** | Victoria Day (May 22) | Victoria Day is always on the Monday preceding May 25. |
| **Jul 1 – Jul 3** | Canada Day (observed on Monday, Jul 3) | Canada Day falls on Saturday; the observed day is Monday, creating a 3‑day break. |
| **Sep 2 – Sep 4** | Labour Day (Sep 4) | Labour Day is always on the first Monday in September. |
| **Oct 7 – Oct 9** | Thanksgiving (Oct 9) | Thanksgiving is always on the second Monday in October. |
| **Nov 9 – Nov 11** | Remembrance Day (Nov 11) | Remembrance Day is always on the Monday nearest to November 11. |
| **Dec 23 – Dec 25** | Christmas (Dec 25) | Christmas falls on Monday; the preceding weekend gives a 3‑day break. |

**Quick summary of the long‑weekend dates (2023)**  

- **Jan 1 – Jan 3** (New Year’s Day)  
- **Apr 7 – Apr 9** (Good Friday to Easter Monday)  
- **May 20 – May 22** (Victoria Day)  
- **Jul 1 – Jul 3** (Canada Day)  
- **Sep 2 – Sep 4** (Labour Day)  
- **Oct 7 – Oct 9** (Thanksgiving)  
- **Nov 9 – Nov 11** (Remembrance Day)  
- **Dec 23 – Dec 25** (Christmas)

Feel free to let me know if you’d like provincial holidays added or if you need the information in a different format (JSON, CSV, etc.).
